title: I've only just got in
goal: Arrive late at the office and catch up with Maryam: who has just done what
tip: taww- 'just' always takes an ending: tawwni 'I've just', tawwak 'you've just', tawwah 'he's just', tawwha 'she's just'. It usually comes before a participle: tawwni wāṣil 'I've just arrived', tawwah ṭāliʿ 'he's just come out'. tawwni adri: 'it's the first I've heard'.
dialogue: A
صباح الخير! توك ياي؟
ṣabāḥ il-khēr! tawwak yāy?
Morning! Have you only just got in?
B
صباح النور. هيه، توني واصل. زحمة وايد!
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. hē, tawwni wāṣil. zaḥma wāyid!
Morning. Yes, I've just arrived. The traffic's terrible!
A
ترا المدير يبيك. توه طالع من الاجتماع
tara l-mudīr yabīk. tawwah ṭāliʿ min il-ijtimāʿ
The manager wants you, by the way. He's just come out of the meeting.
B
أي اجتماع؟ محد قال لي!
ay ijtimāʿ? maḥḥad gāl-li!
What meeting? Nobody told me!
A
شوف تلفونك. الرسالة توها واصلة
shūf tilifōnak. ir-risāla tawwha wāṣla
Check your phone. The message has only just come through.
B
صح! توني أدري. عيل بروح له الحين
ṣaḥḥ! tawwni adri. ʿayal barūḥ-lah il-ḥīn
You're right! It's the first I've heard. I'll go and see him now, then.
A
يلا بسرعة، شكله يترياك
yalla b-surʿa, shaklah yitrayyāk
Quick, then, he seems to be waiting for you.
items: before a participle or a past verb: tawwni wāṣil; Kuwait: the same
I've just arrived (said by a man)
a woman says: tawwni wāṣla (توني واصلة)
have you only just got here? (to a man)
to a woman: tawwich yāya? (توج ياية؟)
he's just gone out, he's just come out
about a woman: tawwha ṭālʿa (توها طالعة)
(she, it) has only just arrived (a woman or a feminine noun: a message)
about a man or a masculine noun: tawwah wāṣil (توه واصل)
it's the first I've heard, I've only just found out
I'll go and see him, I'll go to him
the traffic's terrible, it's really crowded

title: Still at the library?
goal: Phone Sēf late in the evening: he's still studying and still hasn't eaten
tip: lil-ḥīn means 'still': lil-ḥīn fi l-jāmʿa? 'still at uni?'. Before ma and a past verb it means 'still not, not yet': lil-ḥīn ma khallaṣt 'I still haven't finished', lil-ḥīn ma tʿashshēt? 'haven't you had dinner yet?'. Kuwaitis say it the same way.
dialogue: B
ألو سيف، وينك؟ للحين في الجامعة؟
alō Sēf, wēnak? lil-ḥīn fi l-jāmʿa?
Hello Sēf, where are you? Still at uni?
A
هيه، في المكتبة. للحين ما خلصت
hē, fi l-maktaba. lil-ḥīn ma khallaṣt
Yes, in the library. I still haven't finished.
B
الساعة عشر! والمكتبة للحين مفتوحة؟
is-sāʿa ʿashr! w il-maktaba lil-ḥīn maftūḥa?
It's ten o'clock! And the library's still open?
A
هيه، أيام الامتحانات مفتوحة لين نص الليل
hē, ayyām il-imtiḥānāt maftūḥa lēn nuṣṣ il-lēl
Yes, during exams it's open till midnight.
B
وانت للحين ما تعشيت؟
w inta lil-ḥīn ma tʿashshēt?
And you still haven't had dinner?
A
لا، ماني فاضي. للحين ما كلت ولا شي!
la, māni fāẓi. lil-ḥīn ma kalt wala shay!
No, I haven't had time. I still haven't eaten a thing!
B
عيل بييب لك عشا. أنا ياي!
ʿayal bayīb-lak ʿasha. ana yāy!
Then I'll bring you dinner. I'm on my way!
items: still not, not yet (before a past verb)
lil-ḥīn ma wiṣal = he hasn't arrived yet
I still haven't finished; you still haven't finished? (to a man)
to a woman: lil-ḥīn ma khallaṣti? (للحين ما خلصتي؟)
haven't you had dinner yet? (to a man)
to a woman: lil-ḥīn ma tʿashshēti? (للحين ما تعشيتي؟); tʿashshēt = I had dinner
I'm on my way, I'm coming (said by a man)
a woman says: ana yāya (أنا ياية)

title: You should have told me!
goal: Complain, lightly, that Sēf went to the desert without you, and get a promise for next time
tip: chān + a past verb looks back at what didn't happen: chān gilt-li! 'you should have told me!', chān yīt 'I'd have come'. Between friends it's a light complaint, and you can answer ṣaḥḥ, ghalṭati 'true, my fault'. Also: lēsh ma gilt-li? 'why didn't you tell me?'
dialogue: A
هلا! شفت الصور؟ ترا رحنا البر أمس
hala! shift iṣ-ṣuwar? tara riḥna l-barr ams
Hi! Have you seen the photos? We went to the desert yesterday.
B
هلا فيك. رحتوا البر؟ ليش ما قلت لي؟
hala fīk. riḥtu l-barr? lēsh ma gilt-li?
Hi. You went to the desert? Why didn't you tell me?
A
آسف يا ريّال، والله نسيت
āsif yā rayyāl, wallāh nisēt
Sorry, mate, I honestly forgot.
B
جان قلت لي! جان ييت وياكم
chān gilt-li! chān yīt wiyyākum
You should've told me! I'd have come with you.
A
صح، غلطتي. جان خبرتك من أول
ṣaḥḥ, ghalṭati. chān khabbartak min awwal
True, my fault. I should have told you before.
B
ماشي. بس المرة الياية لا تنسى!
māshi. bas il-marra l-yāya la tinsa!
OK. But don't forget next time!
A
ما بنسى، بقول لك. وعد!
ma bansa, bagūl-lak. waʿd!
I won't forget, I'll tell you. Promise!
items: you should have told me (to a man)
to a woman: chān giltī-li (جان قلتي لي); to a group: chān giltū-li (جان قلتوا لي); Kuwait: the same, you'll see written چان
why didn't you tell me? (to a man)
to a woman: lēsh ma giltī-li? (ليش ما قلتي لي؟)
I'd have come, I would have come
chān yīt wiyyākum = I'd have come with you
I should have told you, I should have let you know (to a man)
to a woman: chān khabbartich (جان خبرتج)
I forgot; you forgot (to a man)

title: Sēf's Emirati words
goal: Understand Sēf when he speaks the way Emiratis do at home, and accept his invitation to meet his family
tip: Emiratis often use local forms. Sēf's il-ḥīna basīr is il-ḥīn barūḥ 'I'm going now'; abā, tabā = abi, tabi; hub = mub; yirmis = yitkallam 'speaks'; yālis = gāʿid 'sitting, -ing'; ummāya = ummi 'my mum'. Learn to understand them all, and keep using the forms you know.
grammar: Emirati alternatives (UAE): abā, tabā, hub, il-ḥīna, basīr, yirmis, yālis
culture: In Emirati dialect novels, abā is almost as common as abi, and basīr nearly as common as barūḥ, while Kuwaiti writers hardly ever use them. You'll also hear ʿasab (عسب) for ʿashān 'because, so that'. Some Emiratis frown on it as a newer habit, so just recognise it.
dialogue: A
الحينه بسير البيت. تبا تيي وياي؟
il-ḥīna basīr il-bēt. tabā tiyi wiyyāy?
I'm heading home now. Do you want to come with me?
B
ما فهمت. عيد مرة ثانية، شوي شوي
ma fhimt. ʿīd marra thānya, shwayy shwayy
I didn't get that. Say it again, slowly.
A
يعني الحين بروح البيت. تبي تيي وياي؟
yaʿni l-ḥīn barūḥ il-bēt. tabi tiyi wiyyāy?
I mean: I'm going home now. Do you want to come with me?
B
آه، فهمت! زين عيل. أهلك في البيت؟
ā, fhimt! zēn ʿayal. ahlak fi l-bēt?
Ah, got it! OK, then. Is your family at home?
A
هيه، أمايه يالسة في الصالة، بس تبا تشوفك
hē, ummāya yālsa fi ṣ-ṣāla, bas tabā tshūfak
Yes, my mum's sitting in the living room, but she wants to see you.
B
ماشي، بس أنا أتكلم عربي شوي
māshi, bas ana atkallam ʿarabi shwayy
OK, but I only speak a little Arabic.
A
هب مشكلة، ترا أبويه يرمس انقليزي. يلا، ما أبا أتأخر
hub mushkila, tara ubūya yirmis ingilīzi. yalla, ma abā atʼakhkhar
No problem, my dad speaks English. Come on, I don't want to be late.
items: the default is il-ḥīn (الحين); both are fine
the default is barūḥ (بروح); binsīr (بنسير) = we'll go
do you want? (to a man); she wants (UAE)
to a woman: tabīn? (تبين؟), as everywhere; the default is tabi (تبي)
the default is abi (أبي); ma abā = I don't want
the default is ummi (أمي); my dad: ubūya (أبويه)
a woman: yālsa (يالسة); the default is gāʿid (قاعد); yālis yirmis = he's talking
the default is mub (مب); hub mushkila = no problem
the default is yitkallam (يتكلم); tirmis = you talk, she talks

title: Checkpoint 2.5: the meeting nobody told me about
goal: Checkpoint: Maryam has just come back from a meeting you missed; ask what happened and complain, lightly, that she didn't call
tip: To a woman, taww- takes -ich (tawwich yāya?) and every past 'you' verb ends in -ti: lēsh ma giltī-li? 'why didn't you tell me?', chān daggēti ʿalay 'you should have called me'. 'We've just' is tawwna + a plural participle: tawwna wāṣlīn.
grammar: checkpoint 2.5: recycle s2u073–s2u088 (taww-, lil-ḥīn, chān, discourse markers, negatives)
dialogue: B
هلا مريم! توج ياية؟
hala Maryam! tawwich yāya?
Hi Maryam! Have you just got in?
A
هلا فيك. هيه، تونا واصلين من اجتماع ويا المدير
hala fīk. hē, tawwna wāṣlīn min ijtimāʿ wiyya l-mudīr
Hi. Yes, we've just got back from a meeting with the manager.
B
اجتماع؟ عن المشروع؟ ليش ما قلتي لي؟
ijtimāʿ? ʿan il-mashrūʿ? lēsh ma giltī-li?
A meeting? About the project? Why didn't you tell me?
A
ترا طرشت لك رسالة الصبح!
tara ṭarrasht-lak risāla ṣ-ṣubḥ!
I did send you a message this morning, you know!
B
والله؟ للحين ما وصلتني. محد قال لي شي
wallāh? lil-ḥīn ma wiṣlatni. maḥḥad gāl-li shay
Really? It still hasn't reached me. Nobody told me anything.
A
شكله من الشبكة. المهم، المدير يسأل عنك
shaklah min ish-shabaka. il-muhimm, il-mudīr yisʼal ʿannak
It must be the network. Anyway, the manager's asking for you.
B
زين، بروح له. بس جان دقيتي علي!
zēn, barūḥ-lah. bas chān daggēti ʿalay!
OK, I'll go and see him. But you should've called me!
items: have you only just got here? (to a woman)
to a man: tawwak yāy? (توك ياي؟)
we've just arrived, we've just got back
they've just arrived: tawwhum wāṣlīn (توهم واصلين)
why didn't you tell me? (to a woman)
to a man: lēsh ma gilt-li?
it still hasn't reached me (a message, a parcel)
for a masculine noun: lil-ḥīn ma wiṣalni (للحين ما وصلني)
(he)'s asking for you, asking about you (to a man)
to a woman: yisʼal ʿannich (يسأل عنج)
you should have called me (to a woman)
to a man: chān daggēt ʿalay (جان دقيت علي)

title: A2 exit: my family, my home, my studies and my job
goal: A2 exit: in Bū Rāshid's majlis, tell him about your studies, internship, family and where you live
tip: Answer an elder in short, full sentences and add yā ʿammi. akbar wāḥid 'the eldest' works like aḥsan wāḥid. atdarrab is 'I'm doing an internship, I'm training'. To allāh ywaffigak 'good luck, God grant you success', answer āmīn.
grammar: A2 exit: describe my family, living conditions, education and job
dialogue: A
يا ولدي، شو تسوي هالأيام؟ تدرس ولّا تشتغل؟
yā wildi, shu tsawwi hal-ayyām? tidris walla tishtaghil?
Son, what are you up to these days? Do you study or work?
B
الثنين يا عمي. أدرس هندسة، وأتدرب في شركة
ith-thnēn yā ʿammi. adris handasa, w atdarrab fi sharika
Both, uncle. I study engineering, and I'm doing an internship at a company.
A
ما شاء الله، الله يوفقك. وأهلك للحين في لندن؟
mā shāʼ allāh, allāh ywaffigak. w ahlak lil-ḥīn fi Landan?
Good for you, I wish you every success. And is your family still in London?
B
آمين. هيه، عندي ثلاث إخوان وأخت هناك، وأنا أكبر واحد
āmīn. hē, ʿindi thalāth ikhwān w ukht hnāk, w ana akbar wāḥid
Amen. Yes, I have three brothers and a sister there, and I'm the eldest.
A
وانت هني ساكن بروحك؟
w inta hni sākin b-rūḥak?
And here, do you live on your own?
B
لا أبد، ساكن ويا ربيعي في مردف. والإيجار غالي!
la abad, sākin wiyya rbīʿi fi Mirdif. w il-ījār ghāli!
No, not at all, I live with my friend in Mirdif. And the rent's expensive!
A
هيه والله، كل شي غالي هالأيام
hē wallāh, kill shay ghāli hal-ayyām
Yes, honestly, everything's expensive these days.
items: kill shay ghāli hal-ayyām = everything's expensive these days
do you study or work? (to a man)
to a woman: tidrisīn walla tishtaghlīn? (تدرسين ولّا تشتغلين؟)
I'm doing an internship, I'm training
good luck, God grant you success (to a man)
to a woman: allāh ywaffigich (الله يوفقج); reply: āmīn (آمين)
